title: Circumcision on the Eighth Day (the Covenant Sign)
kjv_text: Every man child among you shall be circumcised... And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you... and my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant. And the uncircumcised man child... that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.
summary: Every male is circumcised on the eighth day as the physical token of the covenant; the uncircumcised is 'cut off' — excluded from the covenant people.
original_audience: Abraham and his household, then all Israelite males 'in your generations,' including slaves 'bought with money.'
immediate_context: God's covenant with Abraham (Gen 17); the sign is given before Isaac is born, binding the seed in the flesh.
historical_context: Circumcision was practiced across the ancient Near East (Egypt, Edom, Ammon) but Israel made it the covenant marker and moved it to the eighth day of infancy — before consent, before memory. It became the boundary of belonging: the Maccabean crisis and Paul's circumcision controversy (Gal 5) both turn on it. 'Cut off' (karet) is the same idiom used for sabbath-breaking and eating leaven in the holy week.
penalty: Being 'cut off from his people' — covenant exclusion, the loss of belonging itself.
exceptions: None in the Old Testament. The New Testament church (Acts 15, Galatians) releases Gentile believers from it — the founding Christian argument the USOC must suppress to keep it mandatory.
nt_passages: Acts 15:1-29 — the Jerusalem Council frees Gentiles from circumcision
Galatians 5:2-6 — 'if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing'
Romans 2:29 — circumcision 'of the heart, in the spirit'
Colossians 2:11 — a spiritual circumcision 'made without hands'
Luke 2:21 — Jesus circumcised the eighth day

internal_contradictions.issue: The Old Testament makes circumcision an 'everlasting covenant' and Paul makes it spiritually void (Gal 5:2, Rom 2:29) — the USOC keeps the flesh and buries the spirit, the reverse of its own New Testament.

usofc_implementation: The covenant sign is the male citizenship record. Eighth-day circumcision is administered and logged by the Bureau of Ritual Cleanliness at birth registration; the certificate is the boy's papers. An uncircumcised male is 'cut off' in the modern sense — no ration card, no school enrollment, no inheritance, no Manna account, no legal personhood. Parents who delay past the eighth day face a sanctity-score penalty; refusal is treated as renouncing citizenship on the child's behalf.
constitutional_analogue: Turns a religious rite into the equivalent of a birth certificate / Social Security number; collides with any secular notion that legal personhood is unconditional at birth.
scene_ideas: The youngest son's eighth-day registration — a warm family rite that is also the state taking its first, permanent claim on him.
A hospital clerk explaining, gently, that an un-registered (uncircumcised) infant boy cannot be issued a ration card — the family's first taste of 'cut off.'
A convert family from a non-circumcising tradition discovering their teenage son is a legal non-person.
satirical_uses: The nation that reads Galatians every Sunday enforces the exact circumcision Paul died fighting — and files the reading under 'eschatological counsel.'
bureaucratic_uses: Covenant-Sign Certificate as primary male ID
cut-off status flag on the Manna
